# Maintain a personal data inventory

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When collecting personal data or changing systems, suppliers or processing purposes. An owned data-flow and processing inventory with sources, purposes, access, retention and unresolved questions.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Inventory data collection and storage points

agent-runnable


List product, sales, HR, analytics and support systems, data categories and collection sources. Include exports, backups and suppliers and use sample metadata rather than copying sensitive records into the inventory.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Confirm purposes, roles and applicable requirements

human · human approval required


Privacy reviewers identify controller or processor roles, purposes, relevant jurisdictions and required records. Record uncertainties and distinguish a technical data flow from a lawful basis or permission.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Map recipients, access and retention

agent-runnable


Trace transfers, internal access, subprocessors and deletion mechanisms. Identify places where actual behavior differs from contracts or notices and assign owners to verify those differences.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve remediation and the processing record

human · human approval required


The responsible owners review undocumented or excessive processing, access and retention. Route high-risk activity to a privacy-impact assessment and approve changes before production implementation.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile the inventory with ongoing changes

agent-runnable


Link the inventory to vendor and release reviews and test representative data flows. Update ownership and evidence when systems or purposes change and retain a history of material decisions.

- Verify: An owned data-flow and processing inventory with sources, purposes, access, retention and unresolved questions.
- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)
